This expands default execution exposure, but does not itself demonstrate bypass of physical-memory admission or artifact qualification.

FlintAnswerStopConstraint.swift's added head lines 72–92 introduce mask caching and delegate chained-decode eligibility. Comparing with base lines 55–85, scanning masks already depend only on the base state, not stop progress; matched nodes allow only answer EOS. The negative matched key is separated from accepted nonnegative base keys. No local mask collision or new output disclosure is demonstrated.

Material integration questions remain: inspect the SDK change at libs/mlx-swift-lm:1 (889fe3c… to 0349802…), including request/constraint-local cache isolation, handling of negative keys, resource-exhaustion invalidation, and chained redraw/termination after a stop match. Equal scanning masks must not allow the engine to ignore differing wrapper transition states. Validate these contracts against FlintNativeProtocolConstraint and the actual engine implementation, rather than treating docs/architecture/inference.md:2172–2183's equivalence claims as proof. Also reconcile automatic serving width with process/KV admission under concurrent Flint requests.

Relevant boundaries are TB-007 and TB-002; output integrity, cancellation and secrecy relate to T-007, T-010, A-001 and T-041. Surrounding documentation preserves encrypted relay, cache scope, ownership retirement and media limits; its unchanged text does not verify those implementations. No supplied change directly alters attestation, provider credentials, billing, cache crypto or privileged helper controls. The unseen SDK delta is a material coverage limit requiring further review.
